_comment: Spelling points the Zolai style guides address, for the Siamsil Zolai Standard review (docs/ZOLAI_STANDARD.md). Each check lists the guides' positions with page or section references and the spellings to count in the sources. Variants are the guides' own examples; none were made up. A guide with nothing explicit on a point says so: its own text still shows its practice in the counts. 'zsf' = Lian Than Tuang, Zolai Standard Format (2018); 'zokam' = Khoi Lam Thang, Zokam le Zolai, chapter 6 Laigelhzia (ZCLS 2013); 'primer' = Lia Cingsen, Paunam Khenna Leh Kampau Luanzia.

guides.zsf: Lian Than Tuang, Zolai Standard Format (2018)
guides.zokam: Khoi Lam Thang, Zokam le Zolai, ch. 6 Laigelhzia (ZCLS, 2013)
guides.primer: Lia Cingsen, Paunam Khenna Leh Kampau Luanzia

checks.zsf: §17 (p. 18): write joined, 'A pai uhhi', 'Ahi uhhi'; also 'uhhiam', 'uhdiam', 'uhhen'.

checks.topic: Locative 'ah' after a place word: joined or separate
checks.zsf: §17 (p. 18): write 'ah' separate, 'Inntung ah, Zogam ah, Nang kiang ah', because joining makes reading harder.
checks.primer: p. 61-62: one-syllable place words stand alone ('Inn sung'); two-syllable ones are joined: 'kiangah, sungah'.

checks.zsf: §6 (p. 12): 'ii' after a noun ('I mawtaw ii a mei'); §16 (p. 18): the apostrophe may replace 'ii' ('Sangpi' mawtaw'), but in formal writing contractions are better avoided.
checks.zokam: No explicit rule; its own text writes the apostrophe ('Pasian'', 'mi'').
checks.primer: p. 64-65 and 93: possessive is written with an apostrophe ('pasalno' laibu', 'Ka pa' sum'), replacing 'ii', which it calls awkward to read.

checks.topic: Subject marker 'in' after a noun or pronoun: full or contracted to 'n
checks.zsf: §16 (p. 18): 'Kote in' and 'Kote'n' are both shown; in formal writing the full form is better.
checks.zokam: 6.2.3: the subject-marker 'in' stands alone ('Pasian in ki-itna ahi hi'); its own text also writes 'ama'n'.
checks.primer: p. 93: contraction with an apostrophe: 'Amahin / Amah'n', 'Kei-in / Ken'n'.

checks.zsf: No explicit rule; its text writes 'i'.
checks.zokam: 6.2.1 (5): write 'i', not 'ih': 'i nu i pa', not 'ih nu ih pa'.
checks.primer: No explicit rule; its text writes 'ih' in places.

checks.topic: 'le' (and) and 'leh' (if); pairs written as one word
checks.zsf: §6 (p. 10): 'leh' = if, 'le' = and. §12 (p. 15): pairs said together are joined: 'Nulepa', 'Innlelo'.
checks.zokam: 6.2.1 (1-3): conditional 'leh' keeps its 'h'; fixed pairs use 'le' and are joined: 'Nulepa' not 'Nu leh pa', 'Khatlekhat' not 'Khat leh khat'.
checks.primer: p. 62: 'leh' is used for 'and': 'Nang leh kei', 'Thangpu leh Khampite'.

checks.topic: Question words 'hiam' and 'diam' or the spoken 'hia' and 'dia'
checks.zsf: §6 (p. 11): in writing use 'hiam' and 'diam'; 'hia' and 'dia' are speech. (Its §8 table, p. 13, still lists 'Dia?' as the question form.)

checks.zokam: 6.2.4: 'ia' and 'ua' are written as such even where they are said 'e' and 'aw' ('pia', 'khua'); only some personal names write the sound (Kam Khaw Thang, Cin Kho Gin, Vum Ko Hau).

checks.topic: Conjunction 'in' after a word ending in a vowel: hyphen, joined, or separate
checks.zsf: §6 (p. 10): 'in' joining clauses is attached to the word before ('laitakin'); 'in' as a separate verb or subject marker stands alone.
checks.zokam: 6.2.3: the conjunction 'in' is attached to the word before, with a hyphen after a vowel ('Tedim pai-in', 'Japan gallai-in'); imperative and subject-marker 'in' stand alone.
checks.primer: p. 61: attached ('hangin, ciangin'), with a hyphen after a vowel, h, l, or p ('pai-in', 'tu-in'); imperative 'in' stands alone ('Tu in', 'Pai in').
checks.note: Separate 'pai in' and 'tu in' can also be the imperative, which all three guides write separately, so those counts mix two uses.

checks.zsf: No explicit rule; its text writes 'zongh' and 'kizangh'.
checks.zokam: No explicit rule; its text writes 'zong' and 'kizang'.

checks.zsf: §6 (p. 9): 'hing' is short for 'hi ing'; careful writing should use 'hi ing'.
checks.primer: p. 94: the contraction is written with an apostrophe: 'hi ing e = hi'ng e'.

checks.zsf: §14 (p. 16): 'a' before a pronoun or position word is joined ('Amah', 'Atung'); before a verb it is separate. §17 (p. 18-19) writes 'ahi hi', 'ahih manin'.
checks.zokam: 6.2.2: the pronoun 'a' stands alone ('a lawmnu'); the copula 'a' is joined: 'ahi hi, ahih hangin'.

checks.topic: Prefix 'ki-' joined, with a hyphen where it would be misread
checks.zokam: 6.3.4: prefixes are joined; a hyphen where the joined word would be misread: 'ki-um', 'ki-it'.

checks.topic: Long paired expressions joined with a hyphen
checks.zokam: 6.3.7: long paired words are split with a hyphen: 'nungak-tangval', 'annek-tuidawn'.

checks.topic: 'zaw' and 'pen' after an adjective: joined or separate
checks.zsf: §4 (p. 7): joined when they compare: 'hoihzaw', 'hoihpen'; separate 'hoih penpen'.

checks.zokam: 6.3.2: written separately in its examples ('hoih mahmah').
